provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Growing plants experiment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plant beans in cotton.
The pupils should be able to observe plant growth.
Introduction:
We have seen plants outside.
Today we will grow our own plants.
Content:
Put beans on wet cotton.
Watch the roots grow down.
Watch the shoot grow up.
Add water every day.
Draw what you see.
Class activity:
Each pupil plants a bean in cotton.
Place on classroom window sill.
Evaluation questions:
What do beans need to grow?
What grows first the root or shoot?
Draw your growing bean plant.
Summary:
Beans grow when we give them water.

topics.title: What plants need
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list what plants need.
The pupils should be able to explain why plants need sunlight.
Introduction:
Last week we planted beans.
Plants need things to grow well.
Content:
Plants need water to drink.
Plants need air to breathe.
Plants need sunlight for food.
Plants need soil to stand in.
One pot in dark place.
One pot in sunny place.
Which one grows better?
Class activity:
Put bean plants in two places.
Water both plants every day.
Draw them after three days.
Evaluation questions:
What do plants need to grow?
Where should we put plants?
Why do plants need sunlight?
Summary:
Plants need water air sunlight and soil.

topics.title: Insects small and busy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify common insects.
The pupils should be able to explain what ants do.
Introduction:
We see small animals around us.
They are called insects.
Content:
Ants work together.
Bees make honey.
Butterflies fly from flower to flower.
Insects have six legs.
Insects are small but busy.
Watch ants march in a line.
Class activity:
Go outside to find insects.
Count how many legs they have.
Draw an insect you see.
Evaluation questions:
Name three insects we see.
How many legs do insects have?
What do ants do together?
Summary:
Insects are small animals with six legs.

topics.title: Water in our life
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list uses of water.
The pupils should be able to explain why we should not waste water.
Introduction:
We use water every day.
Water is very important for us.
Content:
We drink water when we are thirsty.
We use water to wash our hands.
We use water to cook our food.
We use water to bathe.
Do not leave taps running.
Water is precious.
Class activity:
Pupils demonstrate washing hands.
Turn tap on and off properly.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use water for?
What happens if we waste water?
How can we save water at home?
Summary:
Water is useful but we must not waste it.

topics.title: Magnet magic
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify magnetic materials.
The pupils should be able to use a magnet to pick up objects.
Introduction:
Some things stick to magnets.
Today we will test things.
Content:
A magnet can pick up pins.
A magnet can pick up nails.
A magnet cannot pick up wood.
A magnet cannot pick up paper.
Sort magnetic and non magnetic things.
Magnets have two ends.
Class activity:
Give each pupil a magnet.
Test classroom objects.
Put magnetic things in one box.
Evaluation questions:
What can a magnet pick up?
What can a magnet not pick up?
Name something magnetic at home.
Summary:
Magnets stick to some things but not others.

topics.title: Push and pull
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate pushing and pulling.
The pupils should be able to identify push and pull actions.
Introduction:
We use force to move things.
Force can be push or pull.
Content:
Push means to something away.
Pull means to bring something closer.
Push the classroom door to open.
Pull the drawer to open it.
Play push and pull games.
Class activity:
Pupils line up.
Push a ball across the room.
Pull the ball back to start.
Evaluation questions:
What is pushing?
What is pulling?
Show me how to push a door.
Summary:
Push and pull are ways to move things.

topics.title: Light and shadow
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make hand shadows.
The pupils should be able to explain how shadows are formed.
Introduction:
We see shadows when sunny.
Today we make shadows with torch.
Content:
Light travels in straight lines.
When light hits something it makes a shadow.
Shadows are dark shapes.
Shadows follow the light.
Make hand shadows with torch.
Class activity:
Turn off classroom lights.
Use torch to make hand shadows.
Make shadow of a dog bird.
Evaluation questions:
What makes a shadow?
Where do shadows come from?
What animal shadow can you make?
Summary:
Light makes shadows when something blocks it.

topics.title: Floating boat craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a boat that floats.
The pupils should be able to test what makes a boat sink.
Introduction:
Some things float on water.
Today we make boats.
Content:
Make a boat from paper.
Put the boat in water.
If it floats it is good.
Add small stones to boat.
When boat sinks it is too heavy.
Which load sinks my boat?
Class activity:
Each pupil makes a paper boat.
Test boat in basin of water.
Add one coin at a time.
Count coins before sinking.
Evaluation questions:
How do we make a boat float?
What happens when we add load?
How many coins can your boat hold?
Summary:
Boats float until they are too heavy.

topics.title: Weather chart
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different types of weather.
The pupils should be able to mark the weather daily.
Introduction:
The weather changes every day.
We will learn about weather.
Content:
Sunny weather has bright sun.
Cloudy weather has grey clouds.
Rainy weather has falling water.\ windy weather has moving air.
Mark the weather every morning.
Class activity:
Make a weather chart for classroom.
Each day draw the weather.
Say if hot or cold or rainy.
Evaluation questions:
Name three types of weather.
What is the weather today?
What do we wear when sunny?
Summary:
Weather changes and we can mark it every day.

topics.title: Revision and young scientists day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to talk about what they learned.
The pupils should be able to show their plant or boat.
Introduction:
We have learned many things.
Today we share what we know.
Content:
Show my plant that grew.
Show my boat that floated.
Talk about what I discovered.
Be a young scientist today.
Ask questions about experiments.
Class activity:
Each pupil shows their work.
Tell one thing learned.
Give a clap for friends.
Evaluation questions:
What did you like learning most?
What did you grow in cotton?
How does a magnet work?
Summary:
We are all young scientists now.
